subject.title: [RFC] Agent Teleconference — minimum-viable scoped meeting primitive with working prototype

question: Should OpenClaw sponsor a core agent teleconference lifecycle primitive now, or route this capability to plugin/ClawHub or a broader multi-agent architecture track first?
rationale: The current code has enough lower-level delivery/session primitives to prototype this, but the requested core CLI, storage, transcript, config, and cross-agent authorization surfaces are product and security choices that automation cannot safely decide.

options.title: Sponsor a scoped core RFC-to-PR
options.body: Keep this issue open and ask for a narrow design/PR that layers on current session delivery while resolving SQLite/artifact storage, transcript privacy, authorization, and handoff composition first.

options.title: Route to plugin or ClawHub first
options.body: Ask for the teleconference prototype to ship as a plugin/bundle unless it identifies a missing plugin API that must be added to core.

options.title: Defer under broader multi-agent architecture
options.body: Use https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/35203 as the product umbrella and keep this issue as supporting evidence rather than accepting a standalone phase-one surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a scoped core RFC-to-PR
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and ask for a narrow design/PR that layers on current session delivery while resolving SQLite/artifact storage, transcript privacy, authorization, and handoff composition first.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete provided the prior scoped direction on this issue and has adjacent session/A2A history in the relevant code paths.
